name: TikZ
comment:
The grammar for a .tikz file: a figure that is picture body from the first line, with no \begin{tikzpicture} anywhere in it because the caller supplies one. There are no rules of its own here. A fragment is still LaTeX -- % comments, control sequences, \begin{axis} -- so the host grammar does that work, and the two TikZ grammars are injected on top exactly as they are into a .tex file. What the fragment lacks is the tikzpicture scope those injections key on, and that is what the root scope name replaces: it ends in .tikz-file, which the injection selectors name directly, so the whole file counts as a picture body.

The name also has to *start* with text.tex.latex, since scope selectors match by dotted prefix: that is what keeps the existing L:text.tex.latex selector -- and any theme rule written against LaTeX -- applying here without a second clause.
